in_arabic.name: صغيرة
in_arabic.meaning: صغيرة تعني الصغيرة أو القليلة العمر
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم صغيرة مشتق من الصغر، وهو مصدر للصفة 'صغير'، ويعني الشخص الذي يتميز بالعمر القليل أو الحجم الصغير. وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن خلق الإنسان من نطف أمشاج.

in_urdu.name: صغیرہ
in_urdu.meaning: صغیرہ کا مطلب ہے چھوٹی یا کم عمری
in_urdu.long_meaning: صغیرہ نام عربی زبان کے 'صغر' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے 'چھوٹا' یا 'نوجوان'۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ صفت اللہ کے ایک منفرد گুਣ کو ظاہر کرتی ہے۔ اس نام کی روحانی اہمیت اس بات میں ہے کہ یہ اللہ کی قدرت و توانائی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: सगीरा
in_hindi.meaning: सगीरा का अर्थ है छोटी या कम उम्र
in_hindi.long_meaning: सगीरा नाम अरबी भाषा के 'सग़र' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है 'छोटा' या 'नौजवान'। इस नाम का महत्व इस्लामी संस्कृति में है क्योंकि यह अल्लाह की एक विशेषता को प्रकट करता है। सगीरा नाम की आध्यात्मिक महत्वता इस बात में है कि यह अल्लाह की शक्ति और सामर्थ्य को प्रकट करता है।

in_pashto.name: صغیرہ
in_pashto.meaning: صغیرہ معنی یې کوچنی یا کم عمره
in_pashto.long_meaning: صغیرہ نوم د عربی ژبې د 'صغر' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې 'کوچنی' یا 'ځوان' دی. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو لپاره ډیر اهمیت لري او اکثره د اناثو لپاره کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Saghira
in_english.long_meaning: The name Saghira originates from the Arabic root 'صغر' (s-gh-r), meaning 'small', 'little', or 'young'. It is used to describe someone or something of a smaller size or younger age. In Islamic tradition, the name reflects a divine attribute and symbolizes humility and modesty. Historically, the term has been used in various contexts within Islamic literature and theology.

data.cultural_impact: The name Saghira holds a special significance in Islamic culture, particularly in the context of the Prophet Muhammad and his beloved wife, Aisha (RA), who was affectionately known as 'Saffiyah Ukhra' or 'Saghira', meaning 'the little one' or 'the rare one'. The term is also found in the Quran in Surah Al-Azhin, where Allah calls the believers 'Ash-Shakhshiyyah' meaning 'The devoted servants of Allah' and 'Al-Mutahharun', meaning 'The purified ones'. Those who strive to emulate these qualities of loyalty, devotion and purity to Allah may find Saghira as an inspiration and reminder of their commitment.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Saghira holds deep spiritual significance as well, representing two important aspects. First, it signifies a sense of humility and devotion to Allah, reminding us of our smallness and insignificance compared to the greatness of the Creator. The name encourages us to submit ourselves completely to Allah and seek his mercy and blessings. Secondly, 'Saghira' can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of soul growth and spiritual development. Just as a small seed can grow into a large tree with the right nurturing and care, so too can we, as small beings in this vast universe, grow spiritually and achieve great things through dedicated practice and seeking knowledge. The name Saghira inspires us to strive for spiritual growth and to always remember our connection to the Divine.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (The Beginning and the End) - Vol 1, Page 162 The name Saghira carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Kathir narrates the story of a woman named Asma bint Abu Bakr (R) who was known as Saghira. She married the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when she was six years old and consummated the marriage when she was nine. This incident is a subject of controversy among scholars.

historical_references.reference: The Life of Muhammad: A Translation of Ibn Ishaq's Sirat Rasul Allah, with Introduction and Notes by Alfred Guilloum
historical_references.context: Ibn Ishaq describes Saghira as the wife of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who was given to him by her father, Abu Bakr (R), when she was a child. Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet (PBUH) married her when she was six or seven and consummated the marriage when she was nine.
